summary: A long feed of 1000px-wide raster panels for an experimental single-line pattern font, alternating tomato-red and mint full-bleed bands: alphabet posters per weight, cheeky posters ('Using this typeface under 72pt is at your own risk'), product mockups, a decoded character set and a lowercase 'pattern' chapter. The font itself is never live on the page (only Alegreya Sans is loaded); everything is images, so the specimen is a poster wall rather than a tool.

instances.look: On mint, 'WEG' drawn in the font's single red line, which runs off both edges of the frame and tangles into near-illegible shapes, with 'WEG [ve:k]' in bold red Alegreya Sans as the readable key at the right; a small caption 'ONE WAY OF EXPERIMENTATION / Carolina Giovagnoli. March 2021. Last update January 2023.' below
instances.ux: Fixed two-row white nav above (anchors Set / Inspiration / Pattern + external links); no CTA in the hero
instances.learn: When the display face is barely legible, put a plain-type key (name + pronunciation) right beside it so the hero still reads

reconstruction.layout: Header 1000px wide centred (x=220–1220) under an 84px fixed nav; wordmark image ~1000×290 with the line extending to both edges; caption 2 lines at bottom-left, ~16px
reconstruction.typography: Wordmark is an image of Weg Regular (one continuous ~8px red line); key 'WEG' ~60px Alegreya Sans Bold red + '[ve:k]' ~50px Alegreya Sans Light red; caption ~16px Alegreya Sans, first line caps
reconstruction.content: Name, IPA pronunciation, designer and dates

instances.look: On mint: a large italic lead 'WEG* is an experimental pattern-font where legibility isn't the focus.' in the left column, three short first-person paragraphs on the right, then a white box with the dictionary entry '* Weg [ve:k] noun. Path, way, trail, route…' running through Spanish, German and Italian synonyms in monospace
instances.ux: Inline links send readers who need legibility to other HT fonts (Telder, Cira, Kalidoscopio)
instances.learn: Admit the font's limit up front ('legibility isn't the focus') and point to sister fonts for text: honesty that builds trust for an experimental release

reconstruction.layout: 12-col grid inside 1000px: lead in col 1–3 (~230px), text cols 4–12; dictionary blockquote below as a white panel ~1000px wide, ~110px tall, padding ~16px
reconstruction.typography: Lead ~26px Alegreya Sans Italic, leading 1.15, grey; body ~15px Alegreya Sans, one sentence bold; blockquote ~13px Roboto Mono, headword bold, 'noun.' italic, '••' separators between languages
reconstruction.content: Designer statement: single line connecting letters, words and paragraphs; lighter weights are more legible; character set and languages (Spanish, Guaraní, English); multilingual synonyms of 'Weg' (path)

instances.look: Three full-bleed panels, the same uppercase alphabet A–Z (3 lines) in Regular (white line on red), Light (red on mint) and Thin (white on red); the letters untangle as the weight drops
instances.feel: Rhythmic, like flipping through screen prints
instances.ux: static images; no style labels, the change of colour marks each weight
instances.learn: For a line font whose legibility depends on weight, repeat one alphabet per weight on alternating colour panels so the reader sees it untangle

reconstruction.layout: Each panel 1440×667, background colour matching the image; image 1000×667 centred; alphabet in 3 centred lines (A–I, J–R, S–Z.) ~900px wide
reconstruction.typography: Weg Regular / Light / Thin uppercase as raster, cap height ~90px; one continuous line per word
reconstruction.content: Alphabet A–Z plus a full stop
reconstruction.html: article.rojo > figure > img (red panels); article > figure > img (mint panels)

instances.look: Two-colour posters alternating red and mint: 'I'M NOT SURE!' in the line font, 'BUT, THE BIG QUESTION IS: WHERE COULD I USE THIS FONT?' in a box inside a giant Regular glyph, 'USING THIS TYPEFACE UNDER 72PT IS AT YOUR OWN RISK' beside tangled letters, 'TO USE ABOVE 72 POINTS' over a giant filled cut, a cryptic three-line word block beside a huge frame (20), and the giant 'WEG' path wordmark (28)
instances.ux: static images interleaved with the mockups
instances.learn: Let the posters talk about the font's own limits ('under 72pt at your own risk') in a plain bold face: the joke doubles as usage guidance

reconstruction.layout: Each poster 1440×667 full-bleed (1000px centred image on a matching background); compositions put one giant line glyph cropped by the frame against a block of bold sans copy
reconstruction.typography: Weg Regular/Light/Thin as raster line drawings (strokes ~6–30px); commentary in Alegreya Sans ExtraBold caps ~40px, some italic, red on mint or mint on red
reconstruction.content: Self-referential copy about where and at what size to use the font
reconstruction.assets: Weg5, Weg7, Weg8, Weg14, Weg19, Weg27 .jpg posters
reconstruction.html: article(.rojo) > figure > img; HTML comments name each poster ('using this typeface under…', 'to use above 72 pt')

instances.look: Photographic mockups of the patterns and caps on objects: shipping box with 'OLÁ'/'WEG' stickers, a poncho, magazine spread, tote bag + numerals, 'WARTE ZIMMER' wall lettering in a waiting room, three spiral notebooks, a shop window, a matchbox, swing tags, three T-shirts labelled REGULAR / LIGHT / THIN, a wall frieze, a green pillow
instances.ux: static images; the 'Inspiration' nav anchor jumps here
instances.learn: Answer 'where could I use this font?' with surfaces that suit a pattern face (textiles, packaging, signage) rather than text settings

reconstruction.typography: All type inside the photos (Weg line drawings, patterns); no live text

reconstruction.assets: 12 photographic mockups (several from free PSD templates)

instances.look: Introduced by a poster 'I'LL GIVE YOU A LITTLE HINT… IF YOU NEED IT.', then the uppercase set per weight ('WEG Regular / Light / Thin'): A–Z, accented vowels, punctuation and figures, each glyph threaded on one baseline line with its plain letter printed small underneath; then the figures 1–0 at poster size per weight
instances.ux: static images; the 'Set' nav anchor jumps here
instances.learn: Print the plain character under each illegible glyph: the character set becomes a decoder for the reader

reconstruction.layout: Each panel 1440×667; title centred at top; 5 rows (A–M, N–Z, accented vowels, punctuation, 0–9) ~900px wide, each glyph ~55px with a ~10px label below; then three panels of two rows of figures ~250px tall
reconstruction.typography: Titles 'WEG' Alegreya Sans ExtraBold + style name italic ~24px; glyphs raster Weg; labels ~10px sans caps, tracked

instances.look: Chapter 'Beauti—useful typographical pattern set' on white: italic lead at left, a short first-person paragraph on the lowercase 'pattern' stage, a '[ C L I C K H E R E ]' link to the PDF specimen, and a mint box listing the eleven stylistic sets (ss01 Disconnect top … ss09 Disconnected, ss10 Connect Right & Left, ss11 Connect Top & Bottom)
instances.ux: Link opens the pattern specimen PDF; the 'Pattern' nav anchor jumps here
instances.learn: Name stylistic sets by what they do to the connecting line (disconnect top, connect left & right) so the feature list reads as a construction kit

reconstruction.layout: White band 500px; lead col 1–3, text cols 4–12 (~740px); feature list in a mint panel ~740px wide with ~16px padding

reconstruction.content: ss01–ss11 names; the lowercase is a set of connected, combinable patterns in three weights

instances.look: 'WEG LC Regular / Light / Thin': three columns of the lowercase keys a–z, each key letter followed by a strip of its pattern tile repeated, like a swatch book
instances.learn: For a pattern font, show each key as a repeated strip, not a single cell: the reader sees the tile and how it joins its neighbours

reconstruction.layout: Panels 1440×500 on alternating mint/red; three columns (a–h, i–q, r–z) ~180px wide each, ~22px rows, key letter in a ~20px gutter
reconstruction.typography: Title 'WEG LC' Alegreya Sans ExtraBold + style italic ~20px; key letters ~12px; pattern strips raster
reconstruction.content: Lowercase a–z mapped to patterns, per weight

instances.look: Pattern compositions from the lowercase: a profile/hand silhouette carved out of dense line texture, 'THIS IS AN EXTENDED PANGRAM' set beside a block of pattern text, an all-over triangle wallpaper with one plain 'd' key revealed in a box, and a circle-and-bar pattern fading into hatching
instances.learn: Set a pangram in a pattern font and label it: running text becomes a textile, and the label explains what you're looking at

reconstruction.typography: Raster patterns; caption 'THIS IS AN EXTENDED PANGRAM' Alegreya Sans ExtraBold caps ~30px red
